verdict: Dollar General grew sales 5.2% to $11.3B and profit rose by a third, helped by more shoppers in every category, wider margins and a one-off boost from tariff refunds.

kpis.label: Same-store sales
kpis.note: Customer traffic +2.0% and average spend per visit +1.5%

kpis.label: Operating profit
kpis.note: +29% YoY — 6.8% of sales, vs 5.6% a year ago

segments.name: Consumables
segments.note: Food, cleaning, health and other everyday essentials — the core of the store and 82% of sales. Up 5% YoY.

segments.name: Seasonal
segments.note: Seasonal goods, holidays and events. The fastest-growing category, up 7% YoY.

segments.name: Home products
segments.note: Things for the home — kitchen, storage and decor. Up 5% YoY.

segments.name: Apparel
segments.note: Clothing. The smallest category, up 5% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running the stores and the company — staff, rent, depreciation and the back office. Flat as a share of sales at 25.8%.

otherDetail: Other expense was $43M of net interest expense — interest paid on borrowings, net of interest earned.

takeaways.title: Sales grew in every category
takeaways.text: Net sales rose 5.2% to $11.3B. Same-store sales — sales at stores open at least a year — rose 3.5%, from 2.0% more customer traffic and 1.5% more spent per visit, and all four categories grew, led by seasonal at 7.4%. It was the fifth straight quarter of traffic growth.

takeaways.title: Each sale kept more profit
takeaways.text: Gross profit was $3.7B, and gross margin — the share of each sales dollar left after buying the goods — rose to 32.6% from 31.3% a year ago. Tariff refunds added about 81 basis points (0.81 of a percentage point), and distribution costs and the inventory charge known as LIFO were lower, partly offset by more markdowns and higher transport costs.

takeaways.title: Profit rose much faster than sales
takeaways.text: Net income rose 34% to $550M and diluted EPS rose 33% to $2.48, because operating profit jumped 29% to $769M while store running costs stayed flat as a share of sales. Management raised full-year EPS guidance to $7.80–$8.00.

oneTimers: Tariff refunds, after the money Dollar General reinvested from them, added about $0.25 to diluted EPS this quarter and about 66 basis points (0.66 of a percentage point) to operating margin. The company does not expect a material benefit from them in the second half of the year, so this boost should not be treated as the normal run rate.
footerNote: Reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M. Consumables is shown as $9,262M (exact $9,263.0M) so the categories add up to net sales.
